chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdullah, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) led his companions in the Prayer of Fear during the Battle of Dhat al-Riqa. He divided his companions into two groups: one group remained facing the enemy, and the other remained behind him. He said 'Allahu Akbar' and they said it; he recited and they listened; he bowed and they bowed; he prostrated and they prostrated. Then the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) remained standing, and they completed one rak'ah for themselves. Then some of them greeted the others with peace. Then they went to their companions, remained facing the enemy, and their companions came and stood behind the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). He prayed one rak'ah with them, then sat for the Tashahhud and greeted them with peace. They stood up and completed one rak'ah for themselves, and some of them greeted the others with peace.
ai.seo_question: How did the Prophet Muhammad perform the Prayer of Fear during battle?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* provides the definitive procedural model for Salat al-Khaf, illustrating the Prophet's (SAWW) tactical division of forces to maintain both spiritual devotion and military readiness. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the flexibility of prayer during conflict, where the congregation completes the missed rak'ahs individually after the Imam's final salam, ensuring the prayer's validity despite the divided state.
